name: Street Custom 'Spiderbite' Electrified Barbed Wire Launcher
description: A spring-loaded tube launcher that fires a compressed bundle of electrified barbed wire that expands on release, creating a 3-meter tangle of sharp, shocking wire that wraps around anything in its path. The wire is standard concertina barbed wire crimped to a battery-powered electrode that delivers repeated electrical shocks through the barbs. The weapon is designed to entangle and incapacitate — targets wrapped in electrified barbed wire cannot move without driving barbs deeper into their skin while receiving continuous shocks. Extraction requires cutting the wire, which itself is dangerous due to the live electrical charge. It is a weapon of cruelty more than lethality, and its use is a statement of intent.
specifications:
wire length: 5 meters compressed, 3-meter tangle deployed
launch range: 3-8 meters
barb spacing: 5 cm
electrical charge: 400V through wire barbs
battery life: 10 minutes of continuous discharge
weight: 2.5 kg launcher, 1.2 kg per wire bundle
reload: 15 seconds per bundle
extraction time: 5-15 minutes with wire cutters, if you can touch it
story_hooks: Spiderbite launchers have been deployed as perimeter defense around a Tier 1 refugee camp — the wire tangles are keeping threats out, but they are also keeping people in.
A serial attacker is targeting corporate security patrols with Spiderbites, wrapping individual officers in electrified wire and leaving them for hours before anyone finds them.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist tube launcher resembling a hybrid between a flare gun and an industrial spring mechanism. Aggressive, purpose-built aesthetic with exposed mechanical components. The barrel is a wide, ridged steel tube that flares slightly at the muzzle. Everything about it screams improvised lethality.
physical_description.dimensions: Launcher body: 38cm length, 12cm barrel diameter, 8cm grip width. Overall footprint suggests handheld but requires two-hand operation.
physical_description.weight_description: Heavy and unwieldy in one hand, but balanced for two-handed grip. The weight sits forward in the barrel assembly, making it feel like a sledgehammer with a trigger.
physical_description.primary_material: Welded structural steel frame with hardened steel tube barrel. Battery housing is scuffed aluminum alloy. Spring mechanism is visible through reinforced polymer side panels.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with heavy scoring and oxidation. Patches of rust bloom at welds. Barrel edges are sharp and unfinished. No attempt at polish or refinement—purely functional.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey with charcoal blacks and rust-orange corrosion. Electrical contacts are bare copper. Single accent: thin blue LED status indicator on the grip module.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with grooved channels for two-handed hold. Deliberately rough, almost abrasive—designed to not slip even in blood or sweat. Metal trigger guard is exposed steel.
distinctive_features: Exposed helical spring visible through reinforced polycarbonate side panel
Segmented barrel with pronounced ridging for structural rigidity
Thumb-operated electrical arming switch with raised metal guard
Battery status LED pulsing soft blue when charged
Copper contact leads running from grip module to barrel electrode
Crude pressure gauge mounted on right side showing wire bundle compression
Welded cable loop for tactical sling attachment
Heat scarring around barrel mouth from discharge impact
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crude stamped 'SPIDERBITE' across top of barrel. Street shop serial number etched into grip—hand-scratched, not official. No corporate logos; entirely black-market manufacture.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but deliberately scarred. Users treat it as a tool, not a showpiece. Barrel edges are sharp from use. Electrical contacts show green verdigris from humidity exposure. Wire bundle cartridges show visible heat damage from repeated discharge cycles.
